assumptions: The source-reported theorem concerns a complete q-dimensional-input, K-receiver channel with possibly correlated success flags, equal marginal success p>0, and conditional Bell fidelity at least 1-ε for every receiver; it assumes Kp≥1-δ, 0≤δ<1, and 0≤ε≤1/20.

The comparison object is an exclusive uniform routing channel whose intact input is delivered to one uniformly chosen receiver and whose other outputs are input-independent, with arbitrary correlations among those other outputs.
The depolarizing-memory application is conditional on near-ceiling success p≥(1-δ)4^{-N}; it does not supply the extra receivers or environment to the physical memory user.

The Clifford endpoint reduction twirls a successful logical-qubit subchannel while retaining its classical label, then replaces failure by an orthogonal erasure flag; its stated identity does not restrict adaptive memories or prove the unresolved one-layer limit.

latest_substantive_result.summary: The new source-reported theorem says that if a complete q-dimensional-input K-receiver process has equal success p and conditional Bell fidelity at least 1-ε, with Kp≥1-δ, δ<1 and ε≤1/20, then its normalized Choi state lies within half trace distance δ+2√ε+12ε of an exclusive uniform router; the complete channels are within half diamond distance q times this bound. The bound is independent of K. Its depolarizing-memory application assumes p≥(1-δ)4^{-N}. The report also gives an exact counterexample to one proposed positive-correlation collision bound and a probability-preserving Clifford endpoint reduction, but it does not determine the reliability exponent or s0. This is an additive continuation of the earlier DC quantum-memory family.
